title: IRS Whistleblower Program Improvement Act
summary: The IRS Whistleblower Program pays awards to whistleblowers, tied to the proceeds the IRS collects in the matters they report. This bill makes five changes to that program: the Tax Court must review IRS award determinations de novo, based on the administrative record established at the time of the original determination plus any newly discovered or previously unavailable evidence; whistleblowers may elect to proceed anonymously before the Tax Court unless the court finds a societal interest in disclosure that exceeds the potential harm to the whistleblower; awards accrue interest when the IRS does not provide a preliminary award recommendation notice before a set date; the IRS whistleblower report must include a list of up to 10 top tax avoidance schemes disclosed by whistleblowers; and the attorney's-fee deduction is broadened from section 7623(b) awards to all section 7623 awards.
brief: Makes five changes to the IRS whistleblower award program: de novo Tax Court review of award determinations, an anonymity election before the Tax Court, interest on awards when the IRS delays the preliminary award recommendation notice, an expanded whistleblower report, and a broader attorney's-fee deduction.

top_lines.headline: De Novo Court Review
subs: Tax Court must now review IRS whistleblower award decisions de novo (from scratch)
Applies to petitions pending on or filed after enactment

top_lines.headline: Anonymity and Delays
subs: Whistleblowers may elect anonymity in Tax Court, subject to a societal-interest exception
Interest accrues on awards when IRS misses its preliminary recommendation deadline

top_lines.headline: Fees and Reporting
subs: Attorney fee deduction broadened from one whistleblower award category to all of them
IRS report must list up to 10 top tax avoidance schemes disclosed by whistleblowers

likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Kelly (R-PA) with 5 cosponsors. The de novo review requirement in Section 2 is the provision most likely to draw Treasury and IRS opposition, and the five separate substantive changes each add a distinct point of potential objection.

items.main: Names the Act the "IRS Whistleblower Program Improvement Act," provides that amendments refer to the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, defines "Secretary" as the Secretary of the Treasury or delegate, and sets out the table of contents.
items.detail: Short-title / definitions / table-of-contents section — citation name, code-reference convention, and navigational list; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — De Novo Review of Award Determinations

items.main: Amends section 7623(b)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to require the Tax Court to review IRS whistleblower award determinations de novo.
items.detail: The amendment requires the Tax Court's review to be de novo, based on the administrative record established at the time of the original determination plus any additional newly discovered or previously unavailable evidence. It also strikes "appealed to" and inserts "reviewed by," and changes the paragraph (4) heading from "Appeal" to "Review." Applies to petitions under section 7623(b)(4) that are pending on or filed after enactment.

sections.label: Section 3 — Whistleblower Anonymity Before the Tax Court

items.main: Adds section 7623(b)(6)(D) allowing a whistleblower to elect to proceed anonymously in all Tax Court proceedings under the whistleblower award section.
items.detail: Notwithstanding sections 7458 and 7461, a whistleblower may elect to proceed anonymously before the Tax Court unless the Tax Court finds that a societal interest in disclosing the whistleblower's identity exceeds the potential harm disclosure could cause to the whistleblower. The bill does not define "societal interest." Applies to petitions under section 7623(b)(4) that are pending on or filed after enactment.

sections.label: Section 4 — Modification of IRS Whistleblower Report

items.main: Amends Section 406(c) of division A of the Tax Relief and Health Care Act of 2006 to require the IRS whistleblower report to include a list and descriptions of the top tax avoidance schemes, not to exceed 10, disclosed by whistleblowers during the year.
items.detail: Applies to reports for fiscal years ending after the enactment of this Act.

items.main: Adds Section 7623(b)(7) so that if the Secretary fails to provide a preliminary award recommendation notice before the applicable date, the award includes interest from that date at the overpayment rate under section 6621(a).
items.detail: Interest stops accruing once the Secretary provides the preliminary award recommendation notice. The applicable date is 12 months after all award proceeds are collected and the refund period has expired or liabilities are finally resolved. Takes effect 180 days after enactment, with a special transition rule for awards already past the applicable date.

sections.label: Section 6 — Correction Regarding Deductions for Attorney's Fees

items.main: Amends section 62(a)(21)(A)(i) by striking "7623(b)" and inserting "7623," extending the attorney's-fee deduction from awards under section 7623(b) to awards under the whole of section 7623.
items.detail: Applies to taxable years ending after the enactment of this Act.

underreported.summary: A whistleblower may elect to proceed anonymously before the Tax Court unless the Tax Court finds that a "societal interest" in disclosure exceeds the potential harm to the whistleblower. The bill does not define "societal interest."
underreported.why_unreported: The anonymity election is the headline of Section 3, but the exception that overrides it — a Tax Court finding of "societal interest" — uses a term the bill leaves undefined, so the operative limit on the anonymity election is set by Tax Court discretion case by case.

gaps: The bill requires de novo Tax Court review of whistleblower awards but does not set any deadline for the Tax Court to decide a whistleblower petition.

The bill adds interest when the IRS does not provide a preliminary award recommendation notice before the applicable date, but does not set an affirmative deadline by which the IRS must provide that notice.
The bill broadens the attorney's-fee deduction and changes award review to de novo, but does not address how the deduction is treated when a Tax Court review changes the award amount.

added: Section 7623(b)(6)(D) of the Internal Revenue Code — a whistleblower may elect to proceed anonymously in Tax Court proceedings under the whistleblower award section, absent a Tax Court finding of an overriding societal interest in disclosure
